hypotheses.reasoning: auth-svc was healthy (POST /tokens ok, 20-90ms) until a routine rolling deploy of v4.3.0 drained auth-svc-1, dropping capacity to 3/4 at 11:09:02 (#3114). That small capacity dip caused the first 503s, and account-svc's AuthClient retries them right away with backoff and jitter turned off, up to 4 attempts (#3197, #3371, #3500, #3612). This multiplied the load on auth-svc to 3.2-5x baseline with about 700 requests in flight (#3364, #3590, #3735). auth-svc then shed load with 503 queue-full (#3347), which caused more retries. That loop kept going after auth-svc-1 was back and capacity was 4/4 again at 11:09:40 (#3212), so the 503s are not recovering. edge-proxy's POST /login 503s ('upstream account-svc returned 503, retries exhausted') are the downstream symptom.

The auth-svc v4.3.0 rollout came just before the onset. But the new instance reported ready, the auth-svc errors are load-shedding because of request volume rather than code faults, and successful token issuance continued. So the deploy looks like the trigger rather than a faulty release.

verdict.recommendedAction: Stop the retry storm. Turn on exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget, or a circuit breaker, in account-svc's AuthClient. As a short-term fix, cut its retries to 1, or rate-limit or scale out auth-svc temporarily so the inflight queue can drain. Pause the rest of the auth-svc v4.3.0 rollout until things are stable. The other errors look unrelated and can be handled separately: report-cron's missing pandas, the event-processor poison message msg-992570, and metrics-agent exporter drops.
